title: Evaluating Topic Model on Asymmetric and Multi-Domain Financial Corpus
task: Unsupervised risk extraction from risk sections of annual reports
problem: Topic models on corporate filings face sector imbalance and sector-specific vocabulary, which bias the extracted risk themes; standard metrics do not capture this.
architecture: Comparison of NMF, LDA, prodLDA, s-Scholar and covariate c-Scholar (SCHOLAR with sector metadata); three corpus variants (balanced down-sampled DSB, stratified unbalanced DSU, complete C); two new metrics: coherence imbalance (CoIm) between sectors and ToCo for sensitivity to sector-specific language.

datasets.name: French Financial Corporate Annual Reports
datasets.details: risk sections of 171 documents (Reference Documents 2011-2018, Universal Registering Documents 2019-2020); 4,780 paragraphs (1,335 Banks, 1,077 Insurance, 671 Financial Services); 8 documents annotated with 35 risk labels

key_results: On the complete corpus, c-Scholar has the highest diversity (0.894) and lowest ToCo (0.019) but negative NPMI (-0.053); LDA ToCo is 0.293.
Down-sampling lowers coherence imbalance: CoIm drops from 0.020-0.043 (C) to 0.003-0.012 (DSB) across models.
Authors conclude down-sampling is currently the best correction for sector imbalance, and c-Scholar on the complete data best for diversity and resilience to sector vocabulary.

strengths.text: Introduces metrics for imbalance and domain-language sensitivity that standard coherence and diversity scores miss.
Validates extracted risks with experts and provides an analyst-facing interface.

limitations.text: Corpus collected by the authors may carry selection bias.
Small single-language, single-industry corpus (171 documents); the best-diversity model has negative NPMI.

notes: Two further columns in Table 1 (Purity, I) are not defined in the text read, so they are not reported here.
